name: dcf-aapl-2026-09-12
description: Illustrative AAPL-shaped context for tests. Statement figures are approximate; the news items and the model reply are synthetic and were written by hand because no API key was available when this fixture was created. Re-record against the live API with `npm run fixtures:record`.

profile.name: Apple Inc.
profile.description: Designs and sells smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services including the App Store, cloud storage, payments and subscriptions.

news.title: Apple unveils iPhone 18 lineup, keeps base prices flat
news.summary: Apple introduced four iPhone 18 models at its September event and held US starting prices unchanged from last year, while raising the Pro Max price by $100.

news.title: EU regulators open formal review of Apple App Store fee changes
news.summary: The European Commission opened a formal review into whether Apple's revised App Store terms comply with the Digital Markets Act, a process that can end in fines of up to 10% of global turnover.

news.title: 3 reasons Apple stock could soar this fall
news.summary: An opinion piece arguing new devices and services growth could lift the shares.

news.title: Apple in talks to expand Gemini partnership for Siri
news.summary: People familiar with the matter said Apple is negotiating a multi-year extension of its agreement to use Google's Gemini models in Siri. Terms were not disclosed and no deal has been signed.

news.title: Apple shares rise 2% as tech stocks rebound
news.summary: Apple rose alongside other large technology names as bond yields fell.

news.title: US judge sets 2027 trial date in DOJ antitrust case against Apple
news.summary: A federal judge scheduled the Justice Department's antitrust case against Apple for trial beginning in March 2027.

news.title: TSMC begins volume production of Apple A20 chips on 2nm
news.summary: TSMC started volume production of Apple's A20 processor on its 2-nanometer process, according to people familiar with the schedule.

news.title: Apple reports third quarter results
news.summary: Apple reported quarterly revenue of $97.9 billion, up 4 percent year over year, with Services revenue at an all-time high of $28.9 billion. The board declared a dividend of $0.27 per share.

modelOutput.headline: The valuation rests mainly on the 8.4% discount rate and a terminal growth rate that sits close to it, with the stage one growth assumption running well above Apple's five year trend.
modelOutput.plainEnglish: This estimate depends heavily on how much risk is priced into the discount rate and how fast Apple keeps growing far into the future. Recent revenue and cash flow growth have been much slower than what the model assumes for the next few years.

assumptions.evidence: Revenue growth per year across five periods was 3.28% and free cash flow growth was 1.54%, though trailing twelve month revenue grew 5.8%.
assumptions.reasoning: 7% stage one growth is well above both the five year trend and the recent trailing twelve month pickup, requiring services and margin expansion to keep accelerating.

assumptions.evidence: Terminal growth is set at 2.50% against an 8.40% discount rate, a gap of 5.9 points.
assumptions.reasoning: 2 to 3 percent is a reasonable long run terminal rate, but the engine itself flags terminal value at 71% of enterprise value, so this assumption dominates the result.

assumptions.evidence: Net debt to EBITDA is 0.45x, described as strong, and Apple is a large, established company with no sovereign backstop noted.
assumptions.reasoning: 8.40% seems reasonable for a large, low leverage, high return business, though a large-cap of this quality could arguably support a slightly lower rate.

assumptions.evidence: Engine uses $98.80B, matching fiscal year 2025 free cash flow of $98.80B, while trailing twelve month free cash flow is $116.60B.
assumptions.reasoning: The engine's base is below the more recent trailing twelve month figure, so it is not using the most current, higher cash generation level.

assumptions.evidence: Engine uses 14.84B shares, matching the latest diluted share count reported for the trailing twelve months.
assumptions.reasoning: This matches the most recent reported figure and continues the buyback-driven decline from 15.00B a year earlier.

dominantSensitivity.explanation: With terminal value already 71% of enterprise value and only a 5.9 point gap to the discount rate, small changes in the terminal growth assumption swing the valuation far more than any other input.

confidenceReasons: Terminal value dominates enterprise value at 71%, per the engine's own flagged weakness
